analysis.summary: CPU delivered a clean beat on its own upgraded guidance, with Management EPS of 146.92c beating the February 2026 upgrade of ~144c and well ahead of initial August 2025 guidance of ~140c. The driver was broad-based fee revenue growth across all three core segments — Employee Share Plans (+10%), Corporate Trust (+6%), Issuer Services (+4%) — plus cost discipline and Wells Fargo synergy delivery a year early, which more than offset a modest -1.6% decline in Margin Income as rates fell. Cash conversion was excellent: free cash flow of US$801.2m covered the statutory profit ~1.3x and the balance sheet is almost debt-free at 0.11x net debt/EBITDA. The AU$1.20 total FY26 dividend (+29%) and FY27 guidance for +6% EPS growth to 154c signal management confidence, but the payout leap is partly an acknowledgement that the rate tailwind is now a gentle headwind rather than a boost. The single biggest forward risk is a faster-than-guided rate decline compressing Margin Income, which at US$748.7m still represents ~29% of management revenue and where CPU has hedged only ~50-60% of exposed balances.
analysis.full_analysis:
## Executive summary
- **Clean beat vs own guidance**: Management EPS 146.92c delivered above the February 2026 upgrade of ~144c and materially above initial guidance of ~140c; statutory EPS +3.4% to 106.97c.
- **All three core segments grew**: ESP +10% revenue, +24% EBIT; Corporate Trust +6% revenue, +3% EBIT; Issuer Services +4% revenue, but EBIT -4% as Margin Income fell and investment spending stepped up.
- **Balance sheet transformation complete**: Net debt/EBITDA collapsed from 0.42x to 0.11x following UK Mortgage Services disposal (Feb 2026) and strong cash generation; this funds the 29% dividend increase and future M&A optionality.
- **Margin Income still shrinking but cushioned**: MI fell -1.6% to US$748.7m despite rising average client balances (+US$1.8bn to US$31.7bn) — rate cuts in all major markets were partly offset by hedging and balance growth; FY27 guidance assumes MI rebounds to ~US$770m on an assumed rate increase cycle.
- **Red flag — restructuring costs are persistent**: Major restructuring costs added back to reach management NPAT were US$61.6m in FY26 (US$60.7m in FY25); this is now a recurring 'one-off', and amortisation of acquisition intangibles (US$76.3m net of tax) is also structural.

## Key numbers
| Metric | FY26 | FY25 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Management Revenue (actual rates) | US$3,265.9m | US$3,120.2m | +4.7% |
| Management Revenue (constant currency) | US$3,212.5m | US$3,120.2m | +3.0% |
| Margin Income | US$748.7m | ~US$760.3m est. | -1.6% (CC) |
| Management EBIT | US$1,210.7m | US$1,174.3m | +3.1% |
| Management EBITDA | US$1,284.9m | US$1,244.0m | +3.3% |
| Statutory NPAT (post-NCI) | US$618.7m | US$607.0m | +1.9% |
| Management NPAT (post-NCI) | US$849.8m | US$793.8m | +7.1% |
| Bridge: statutory to management NPAT | Amortisation +US$76.3m; restructuring +US$61.6m; UK MS loss on sale +US$46.3m; UK MS disposal costs +US$32.0m; integration costs +US$10.8m; hedge modification +US$8.6m; less contingent consideration gain -US$5.1m; MTM +US$0.3m | | |
| Statutory EPS (basic) | 106.97c | 103.45c | +3.4% |
| Management EPS (basic, actual rates) | 146.92c | 135.28c | +8.6% |
| Management EPS (constant currency) | 145.19c | 135.08c | +7.5% |
| Free cash flow | US$801.2m | US$780.1m | +2.7% |
| Cash flow from operations (ex-SLS) | US$836.6m | US$823.7m | +1.6% |
| Net debt/Management EBITDA (ex non-recourse) | 0.11x | 0.42x | -0.31x |
| Total assets | US$4,966.7m | US$5,335.4m | -6.9% |
| Total shareholders' equity | US$2,287.4m | US$2,140.7m | +6.9% |
| Return on equity (management) | 38.3% | 38.7% | -40bps |
| Staff numbers | 11,625 | 12,891 | -9.8% |

## Quality of earnings
- **Cash conversion is strong**: Free cash flow of US$801.2m against management NPAT of US$849.8m = ~94% conversion; operating cash flow (ex-SLS) of US$836.6m is essentially equal to statutory NPAT — no obvious working capital inflation.
- **Restructuring is a recurring add-back**: US$61.6m in FY26 (major restructuring) follows US$60.7m in FY25. Two consecutive years of near-identical 'one-off' restructuring charges signal this is a structural cost of running the business. Stripping this out to reach 'management' NPAT flatters the true earnings power.
- **Amortisation of acquisition intangibles**: US$76.3m net of tax added back in FY26 (vs US$70.6m in FY25). These are real economic costs representing the decay of acquired client relationships and technology; the management EPS number permanently excludes them.
- **UK MS disposal losses**: A US$46.3m loss on sale plus US$32.0m disposal-related expenses (US$78.3m combined, net of tax) from the February 2026 UK Mortgage Services sale are legitimately excluded from management results, but represent real cash/value destruction from an exit at below book value — this was a strategic clean-up, not a clean deal.
- **Margin Income hedge modification**: US$8.6m added back (US$19.9m in FY25) relates to fair-value adjustments on interest rate hedges — non-cash but reflects genuine risk management costs being excluded from the headline number.
- **Capitalised costs / DSO**: Detailed DSO and capitalised software disclosure not extracted in the text provided; receivables and inventory granularity limited in this excerpt.
- **Staff reduction of 1,266 headcount** (-9.8%) is consistent with the restructuring charges and cost-out savings; the salary inflation line of US$93.7m partially offsets the headcount reduction benefit.

## Management framing
**Rating: Mixed — mostly transparent with selective emphasis**
- **Transparent**: CPU provides a clear statutory-to-management bridge with named line items and dollar amounts; the amortisation, restructuring and disposal costs are all individually disclosed. Constant currency vs actual rates are both shown. Guidance upgrades are explicitly referenced.
- **Promotional**: The Chairman's report leads with constant currency EPS and Management Revenue rather than statutory numbers — the 107c statutory EPS (barely above the 103c prior year) gets no prominence, while the 145c management EPS is front and centre. The +29% dividend increase is highlighted but not contextualised against the fact that free cash flow growth was only +2.7%.
- **Selective emphasis**: Issuer Services EBIT fell -4.2% (in CC) — this is buried in the CEO's report after the positives; the margin compression from lower MI and higher investment spend in IS is mentioned but framed as a deliberate 'investment' rather than a miss.
- **Restructuring opacity**: Management never explains when restructuring costs will end; US$61-62m per year for two years with ongoing cost-out programs and a FY27 promise of further US$22m savings implies this line continues.
- **Stranded costs**: The FY26 CEO report flags US$33.3m of 'stranded costs' from the US MS disposal, allocated across segments but excluded from segment EBIT in the commentary — this is a legitimate but double-adjusting practice (stranded costs are in the reported segment P&L but excluded from the management EBIT commentary used to calculate management EPS).

## Segments
| Segment | FY26 Revenue (actual) | Change (CC) | FY26 EBIT (ex stranded) | EBIT Margin | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Issuer Services | US$1,310.6m | +4.4% | US$436.5m | 33.3% | -300bps |
| Corporate Trust | US$1,032.0m | +5.7% | US$526.4m | 51.0% | -150bps |
| Employee Share Plans | US$559.7m | +10.2% | US$260.8m | 46.6% | +530bps |
| Corporate & Other | US$310.2m | -18.7% | -US$27.4m | n/m | deteriorated |
| **Group Total** | **US$3,265.9m** | **+3.0%** | **US$1,210.7m** | **~37.1%** | **+0bps approx** |

- **Issuer Services**: Revenue growth driven by US corporate actions volumes (+3% deals, +8% in 2H), Hong Kong IPO surge (+96%), Register Maintenance fees (+3%) and Entity Solutions (+7.7%). But Margin Income declined US$9.1m and the company invested in new product development, compressing EBIT margin 300bps. Net: growing but getting less profitable per dollar of revenue.
- **Corporate Trust**: US$80m Wells Fargo synergy target delivered a full year early — a genuine positive. Trust fee revenue +9%; structured products growing strongly. MI down US$3.1m. EBIT ex MI margin expanded to >17% (as stated by management). The 150bps overall margin decline is entirely MI-driven.
- **Employee Share Plans**: The standout performer. Transaction fees +18% on record trading volumes, assets under administration up 8%, administered units +5%. EBIT +24%, margin +530bps. Volatility in equity markets was a positive for transaction volume. High operating leverage evident.
- **Corporate & Other**: Revenue down US$71.2m driven by UK MS disposal (February 2026) and lower MI. EBIT loss of US$27.4m. Stranded costs from prior US MS disposal also sit here. This segment will mechanically improve in FY27 as comparatives reflect a full year without UK MS.

## Balance sheet
- **Near debt-free**: Net debt/EBITDA of 0.11x (ex non-recourse debt) vs 0.42x a year ago — a dramatic deleveraging. Total assets fell US$368.7m to US$4,966.7m, partly reflecting the UK MS disposal.
- **Equity up 6.9%** to US$2,287.4m, consistent with retained profit after dividends.
- **No covenant or refinancing stress identified** in this excerpt; the low leverage gives material headroom.
- **Non-recourse debt**: SLS (Specialized Loan Servicing) advances and associated non-recourse debt are excluded from the headline leverage ratio — this is standard practice but worth noting as a gross balance sheet item.
- **Capital allocation**: With 0.11x leverage and US$801m FCF, CPU has significant firepower. Management flagged a pipeline focused on Corporate Trust and Entity Solutions acquisitions; patience and discipline emphasised.
- **ROE** dipped 40bps to 38.3% despite higher NPAT — equity base growing faster than profits, suggesting the balance sheet is becoming over-capitalised without a near-term acquisition or capital return event.

## Dividend and capital allocation
- **FY26 total dividend: AU$1.20/share** (+29% on FY25's AU$0.93). Interim AU55c (30% franked), Final AU65c (unfranked).
- The 29% dividend increase significantly outpaces the 7.1% management NPAT growth and 2.7% FCF growth — this is a deliberate policy signal that the balance sheet is strong enough to sustainably uplift the payout ratio.
- **FY25 final was AU48c; FY26 final is AU65c** — a 35% jump in the final dividend alone. This is partly an admission that prior dividends were conservative relative to earnings power.
- **No buyback announced** despite the clean balance sheet; management appears to be preserving M&A optionality.
- **Franking**: The interim was 30% franked; the final is unfranked — reflecting the proportion of Australian-source taxable income. Given ~56% of revenue is US-sourced, full franking is structurally unavailable.

## Guidance and outlook
- **FY27 Management EPS guidance: ~154c** (+6% on FY26 actual of 146.92c).
- **Margin Income forecast: ~US$770m** (vs US$748.7m in FY26) based on: average client balances of US$32.8bn; average yield of 2.35%; assumed rate increases in US (Jan), Canada (Mar), UK (Nov + Mar); hedged proportion rising from ~50% to ~60% of exposed balances.
- **EBIT ex MI: up ~3.5%** (or ~7% adjusting for disposed businesses).
- **Operating cost inflation below 3%** in FY27; additional US$22m cost-out savings by end of FY27.
- **EBIT ex MI margin target: ~19%** for full year.
- **Net interest expense down ~15%** due to lower debt levels.
- **Guidance caveat**: Assumes broadly consistent equity market conditions for ESP transactional revenue; event fees in ESP expected to decline as some FY26-specific activity will not repeat.
- **Risk to guidance**: The MI forecast assumes a rate-increase cycle — this is an unusual assumption in mid-2026 and could easily be wrong if central banks pause or cut further. A US$10m miss on MI would be ~1.2% of management NPAT.

## Positives
- **ESP EBIT +24%** with margin expanding 530bps — high operating leverage demonstrating the business model at its best; US$289bn in assets under administration provides a durable revenue base.
- **Wells Fargo synergies delivered a year early** in Corporate Trust; US$80m target achieved, providing a clean FY27 baseline without integration drag.
- **Balance sheet strength**: 0.11x net leverage with US$801m FCF gives strategic flexibility rare in this peer group.
- **Corporate Actions momentum building through FY26**: US deal volume +3% for the year, +8% in 2H; pending deal count +8% at year-end — a positive leading indicator for FY27 IS revenue.
- **Hong Kong IPO +96%**: Demonstrates geographic diversification value; non-US growth vectors reducing rate-cycle dependency.
- **Dividend +29%** signals management and board confidence in the earnings durability; payout comfortably covered by FCF.
- **Staff headcount -9.8%** while revenues grew — productivity improvement is real and structurally valuable.
- **FY27 MI guidance assumes rate increases** — if correct, removes the rate headwind that suppressed FY26 IS and CT margins.

## Negatives / red flags
- **Restructuring 'one-off' is now recurring**: US$61.6m in FY26, US$60.7m in FY25 — this should be treated as an operating cost, not an add-back. Adjusting for this, true underlying NPAT is ~US$788m, not US$849.8m.
- **Issuer Services EBIT margin fell 300bps** to 33.3% — the largest segment by revenue is getting less profitable; Margin Income headwinds and investment spend are compressing returns without a clear payback timeline disclosed.
- **UK MS disposal at a loss**: US$78.3m total cost (loss on sale + disposal expenses, net of tax) to exit a non-core business. This is a real economic cost, not a footnote.
- **Guidance relies on rate increases**: FY27 MI forecast of US$770m assumes central banks raise rates; if the cycle reverses, MI misses and EPS guidance is at risk given MI is ~23% of management revenue.
- **Management EPS is NOT a GAAP metric and excludes real costs**: Adding back amortisation (US$76.3m) and restructuring (US$61.6m) together total US$137.9m net of tax in FY26 — that is a 22% premium to statutory profit. Investors relying solely on 146.92c are paying for economics that may not fully materialise.
- **ROE trending down**: 38.3% in FY26 vs 38.7% in FY25 — minor but consistent with the over-capitalisation risk as the balance sheet strengthens faster than earnings grow.
- **ESP event fee revenue expected to decline in FY27**: Some FY26 one-off activity will not repeat; this creates a tough comp in the strongest-performing segment.
- **Continental Europe revenue -21.9% in constant currency**: A meaningful regional deterioration; no substantive explanation provided in the text.
- **Stranded cost accounting**: US$33.3m of stranded costs are in the statutory P&L but excluded from segment management EBIT commentary — a legitimate but layered adjustment that makes true segment economics harder to assess.

## Bottom line
**Bull case**: CPU is a capital-light tollbooth on global financial markets with genuinely sticky client relationships, rising recurring fee revenues and a near-debt-free balance sheet. ESP and Corporate Trust are in structural growth phases; the Wells Fargo integration is complete and delivering; the balance sheet funds both a rising dividend and selective bolt-on M&A without equity dilution. FY27 guidance of 154c EPS is conservative if deal volumes hold and rates rise as assumed. On ~17-18x management earnings, the stock is not expensive for this quality.

**Bear case**: Management EPS inflates the true picture by US$137m/year of recurring 'one-offs'. Statutory EPS of 107c grew just 3.4% and is only ~72% of the management number. Margin Income — still US$749m or 23% of revenue — faces structural headwinds if central banks cut rather than hike, as many forecasters expect. Issuer Services margins are compressing. The 29% dividend jump is unsupported by equivalent FCF growth and reduces reinvestment flexibility. At current multiples, the market is pricing in the bull case with limited margin for error.

**What would change the view**: (1) A sustained rate-cut cycle in the US/UK/Canada that takes MI below US$700m would break the FY27 earnings narrative — watch the February 2027 1H update MI line closely; (2) A large Corporate Trust acquisition would test management's discipline claim and could re-lever the balance sheet quickly; (3) If restructuring costs disappear in FY27 (confirming they were genuinely one-off), the statutory-to-management earnings gap would close and the stock's multiple would be better justified.
